subject: sg
title: (R)SG.------TR.
description: First of two diagrams in MP(I)-4 (Multi-Particulars, Level One — sixties activism). The prose facing the diagrams names the structural problem: it would 'not be correct to view the functionalism in this period as a successful revolution by any means. Instead, the real significance of this period might lie in what this junction means for black people as we enter the eighties — that being, the nature of how sixties functionalism has helped to set the stage for transitional functionalism of the second degree.' The crossing diagrams the route the sixties' source-generation actually traveled: (R)SG (reality of source-generation — what the radical political activism of the sixties actually generated) is crossed with TR (transformation — what that generation was supposed to become). SG sits on the left with the subject-arrow; T-C-IMP (time continuum implications) sits centrally as the subject's hub, with MT-DEVF (multiple diversification), IF-SPT (infra-spirituality), and TRS (transition, in its lowercase aspect-form) hanging below — the actual outputs source-generation produced in the sixties. TR rises at top-center as partner-axis; A-PR (all-purpose) anchors the upper-right, with DIS-C-CT (disintegration of a culture's center) and POL-DYM (political dynamics) on the right as the partner's downward outputs. Structural argument: when sixties source-generation is crossed with transformation, the partner-side's downward chain (A-PR → DIS-C-CT → POL-DYM) is precisely the failure-route the prose names — all-purpose terminates in disintegration of a culture's center rather than reaching back to the subject-side's hub. The subject's T-C-IMP holds MT-DEVF/IF-SPT/TRS as time continuum implications, but without the partner-side closing the loop, those implications stay implications. The transformation never reaches the subject's source-generation as actual continuance; the political-dynamics on the partner-right becomes the only output, and that is exactly the political-dynamics the next diagram on this page picks up.
